utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, Daryl Mundis; we're assisted today by our intern Jaspreet Saini, and our case manager Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present: Members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom. We have a new map, and the witness will certainly indicate the positions of units when asked to do so by the Prosecution. If there are no issues to be raised by either of the parties, I will now ask the usher to call General Merdan into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, General. I would first like to make sure that you are receiving interpretation of what I'm saying. It seems so. This is the second week of your testimony. If everything goes as planned, we should conclude your testimony this week. It seems that we have a problem. Can you hear me or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar. Are you receiving the interpretation now or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll change the headphones. Can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, as I was saying, this is the last week dedicated to your testimony, as your testimony should be concluded by the end of the week. We'll start with the cross-examination. There was a problem as far as the maps and position of the units are concerned. I think that we have changed the map. I will now give the floor to Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you were here on Friday, we were discussing the possibility of having you make some markings on a map, and I hope you were informed by the Victims Unit that we have come up with an alternative solution to that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if the usher can be of assistance, I would ask, Mr. President, that the witness be permitted to approach the large map that is now hanging in the courtroom. And if it's possible, I would like the general just to take a look at the map and to then be in a position, hopefully, to answer a few questions about the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I see that you've had an opportunity to look at this map. I would ask you first of all if you can recognise this map; and if so, if you can tell us what this map represents.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness isn't receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you hear anything now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, now that you've had a moment to look at the map, I would ask you if you can recognise the map. And if you do, if you can please tell us what this map represents.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that this is the commanders' working map, dated the 13th of August 1993. And it's Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic's, but I can't see the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you say it's a working map, can you perhaps explain what a working map would be.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a rule, a working map represents the main elements of the deployment of our own forces and of the enemy forces. And the purpose of this map is to enable the commander to follow the situation in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could, if you could look towards the top of the map, you'll note different shades at the very top. Would this be the type of map that some kind of clear overlay would be taped onto the map so that markings could be made on the map and those markings could then be changed as the situation develops on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that at the top there are different shades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also, if you look closely, I believe you can actually see -- this map is a photocopy of a map with an overlay on it. I believe you can actually see where the cellophane tape holds the -- what would have held on the original the overlay onto the actual map. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there's -- sir, let's start, for the benefit of everyone in the courtroom, if you could explain to us the various markings that you see on the map. Perhaps starting with the dashed lines that appear throughout the map, and also indicate to us what the different colours of those lines represent.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an interruption in the interpretation. Could you please repeat your question because I wasn't able to hear the entire question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. There are a number of different types of markings on this map. And some of those markings are actually in different colours. Could you please explain to us these markings and perhaps begin by telling us what the dashed lines represent and also informing us what the colours of those lines represent.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question very well. But if I have understood it correctly, I should tell you what these dashed lines and what these colours, the red and blue and orange colours and the black colours represent. Is that what you're asking me to say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The colour red should indicate the lines of deployment of the aggressor in Bosnia and Herzegovina according to intelligence that was obtained. As to whether this was the actual location of the lines as they're depicted on the map, I can't remember. But this should be where the aggressor was deployed. The colour red indicates the positions at which the aggressor was deployed. Blue should represent the deployment of our own forces. I don't know whether this line was drawn on the same day, the line representing the positions of our forces, the forces of the 3rd Corps. I can see that the forces of other corps are also indicated here. I can't read this very well, I can't read the names of these places very well, but other corps are referred to, not just the 3rd Corps. And the blue colour here within the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, well, again, I can't see the places, the names of the places, Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond and I couldn't say whether this is where our forces were deployed on that day. But blue represents our forces, 3rd Corps forces. I can also see orange or yellow, and this would be the positions at which the HVO forces were deployed. I can't confirm that the HVO was actually deployed at these positions on that day. And then operations groups are indicated in red, operations groups in zones where the relevant operations groups operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there also appear to be some little markings with what appear to be little flags. Can you tell us what those represent.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the map, I can also see such symbols. They represent command places, the corps command place, the command places of operations groups and of brigades. I can see that there are also the command places of municipal staffs here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could turn your attention very briefly to the area in the middle of the map where you indicated the HVO was deployed, the formation in the middle of the map, I would ask you, sir, to look at the southern part of that bubble, if you will. There don't appear to be any lines at the southern portion of the area where the HVO were located. Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the part you are referring to? Or are you referring to some other location?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. No, the part, sir --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right to the south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That part right there where you're pointing to now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps if the cameras could focus on that part of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that area right there, sir. Do you recall what kind of lines or what kind of operations were going -- taking place in that area during the middle of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this area, in mid-1993, there were -- there was combat, but it wasn't large scale. Combat adopt the most favourable combat positions. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, what do you mean by "most favourable combat positions"?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since the ABiH was trying to avoid a conflict with the HVO, the units during that period of time didn't launch any attacks. They only adopted positions for defence. And in this area, there was no combat at the time, no significant combat, especially not for the corps command. Perhaps for the lower level of command and control, for brigade or a battalion, perhaps such a combat did have significance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked that question, sir, because it -- for a layperson, the fact that there are what appear to be confrontation lines, but in that one area there are no such confrontation lines, might lead one to ask why. And I was just wondering if you could perhaps give us any further explanation with a particular focus on confrontation lines in that area.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area is south of Busovaca. It covers the territory of Busovaca Municipality. In mid-1993, in this area, we had ABiH patrols. They would go from Simsir through Busovaca mountain up to Rok. We had patrols here but there weren't any classical, any usual lines. There were no trenches. We didn't have units that were permanently deployed there, which was the case in other areas, but we did have units moving around in this area. And there were some sabotage actions in order to take combat positions. So there were operations, there were troops, but there wasn't fighting as was the case in other areas. I would also like to say that in mid-June, this was a difficult month for the 3rd Corps, so we should be more specific with regard to the time concerned because June was a crucial month for the 3rd Corps as far as combat in Central Bosnia is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, to the best of your recollection, at any point in time in 1993 were there identifiable confrontation lines in the area we've just been talking about where there appears to be a gap in the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I can't remember the exact date. I don't know whether it was in mid-1993. But in the wider area of the Busovaca mountain, there was fighting, there was a combat operation. I can't remember the exact date, but there was one combat operation. I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That completes the questions that I'll be asking you about the map. So perhaps the usher can assist returning you to the witness box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I would certainly ask that this map be given a number for identification purposes. We will be seeking to tender this map, but at least for now, for the record, if it could be given a number marked for identification, we would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar -- Defence counsel, any comments to make with regard to marking this map for identification, a map that the witness has identified?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution informed us on Friday that they would be using this map as a new piece of evidence. And we don't object to having it marked for identification, nor do we object having this map tendered into evidence. So when the Prosecution deems that it is appropriate to do this ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This map will be marked for identification. The number will be P938/ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point in time I would ask that the witness be shown three documents. Two of them -- all three of these documents were among the documents that the Defence notified us that they would be using with this witness. Two of these documents, number 0502 and 0705, were, in fact, shown to the witness. The third document, 1005, was among the binders provided by the Defence, but I do not believe that document was actually shown to the witness. With your leave, we would ask that all three of these documents, including the one which the Defence put on their list but which they did not show the witness, be shown to the witness at this time. And we do, I believe, have sufficient copies of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have three documents; 502, 705, and 1005.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you first to look at Document 0502.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've had a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the third paragraph of this document, I'm wondering if you can elaborate for us on the information contained in the third paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the third paragraph of this document, it says that wearing Croatian Army insignia by individuals is linked to accusations regarding the direct involvement of HV units in the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna, which leads to accusations against the Republic of Croatia and the Croatian Community of Herceg Bosna. Members of the HV are also requested to wear HVO insignia while in our areas. That's what it says in paragraph 3 of this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know anything about what's stated in the third paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if there were, in fact, members of the Croatian Army in Central Bosnia wearing HVO insignia during 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard information according to which there were some Croatian troops in Central Bosnia; that is to say, there were troops from the Croatian Army. I don't know how many of them there were, and similarly I don't know which units were engaged there. But I do know that in this area there were Croatian troops that had been engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask you now, sir, if you could look at, please, Document 0705. And I'm particularly interested in the first sentence of that document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first sentence in this document states the following: "The situation in Gornji Vakuf is a classic example of an occupation by the HVO Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond and the Croatian Army." That's the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any knowledge or can you tell us what is meant by "a classic example of an occupation by the HVO and the HV"?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that HVO units and HV units had attacked Gornji Vakuf. That would be my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you now turn to Document 1005. And again, I would ask you to look at the first paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of May 1993, in the afternoon, a helicopter of the Croatian air force landed in the village of Stojkovici, Novi Travnik. The same happened in Busovaca on the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, other than the two references in this paragraph to Croatian air force helicopters being in the Central Bosnia in May, 1993, were you aware of other instances where the Croatian air force was active in Central Bosnia during 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had some information that the Croatian air force was very intensely engaged in that area at the time. Helicopters dropped materiels and supply to the HVO, including military assistance, mostly by night when visibility was reduced, but the noise of the helicopters was clearly audible and unmistakable, and you could see them dropping parcels in that area. I had, indeed, information that this was done by the Croatian air force using helicopters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I'd now like to turn to a different topic, and that being the importance of observing international humanitarian law. Would it be fair to say, sir, that from the beginning of the war in Bosnia in the spring of 1992, that President Izetbegovic and the top leadership of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina placed a great emphasis on strict adherence to the laws of armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all subordinate units of the ABiH were required to take all the necessary steps to prevent crimes from being punished by soldiers of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The command of the 3rd Corps took a number of steps to train its troops, and I have spoken about it at length. They were trained in order not to break the international humanitarian law. I also mentioned that the soldiers in question had no military education. They were organised hastily, as best we could. And of course, the corps sometimes resorted to disciplinary measures and sanctions against those who violated the discipline and the international humanitarian law. Anybody who was found guilty was held accountable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, I suggest to you that there are two primary reasons why the ABiH placed an importance on the law of armed conflict. The first was because had the state not done so, it would have harmed the reputation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and second, because the failure to take steps to prevent and punish crimes can have a serious detrimental effect on morale and combat readiness. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the kind of information you have, I can only acknowledge that you have such information. I agree with your reasoning. One should bear in mind that the BH Army was the official armed force of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that it was our duty, since we were defending our state, to abide by the international humanitarian law and the laws and customs of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from that, sir, that the leadership of the 3rd Corps, including yourself as the deputy commander and General Hadzihasanovic as the corps commander, took these obligations very seriously, and that would mean that any reports or any information that you obtained that indicated crimes might have been committed would be taken very seriously.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, we'll talk perhaps tomorrow a little bit more about Dusina, but I mention that at this point because you told us last Tuesday that Dusina was a significant event because it was the first time you had received information that an army unit of the 3rd Corps may have possibly committed some kind of war crimes. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received that report at a meeting in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, in part because this was the first time you had received such a report, that you took it very seriously and wanted to leave no stone unturned in terms of finding out what had happened in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of Dusina, we took every step that it was our duty to take. Based on reports from the competent authorities and professionals, including the civilian police, we found out that this case involved the wounding and killing of soldiers in combat activities. Our sources were professionals who were able to evaluate whether the casualties were inflicted in the course of combat activity. And it was their conclusion that it was combat activity, not war crimes or any other crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I said, sir, we will return to the topic of Dusina perhaps tomorrow morning. Let me turn to the issue of the various commission meetings or meetings to discuss cease-fires, the meetings that you held with your counterparts from the HVO that were attended by representatives of the international community, whether the EUMM or BritBat or any other international organisation. You told us that at these meetings both sides would often raise complaints with the other side concerning a number of different issues, but including the treatment of persons who had surrendered or been captured. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only exchanged information on such occasions, and that's what I testified to here. All the information I received from various sources, I would present to them because it was our only line of communication with the HVO. Whether the Croatian Defence Council was able or willing to accommodate my requests is a different issue. But I also said the HVO used that opportunity to provide me with the information they had about any complaints and problems they had so that we could deal with them before they became aggravated and led to incidents, maybe even armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, I assume that you fulfilled your obligations in conveying any such complaints that you received from the HVO to the corps commander, General Hadzihasanovic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of these reports I would indeed share with him. Some I would send down to the local level because they concerned the local level. We were indeed a local commission. The first one that was set up in Busovaca was called the joint committee or commission of Busovaca and it was a forum for dealing with problems in Busovaca at a tactical level together. If an incident would occur in Busovaca itself or at the nearby front line, I would not pass that information up to the command level because it was the tactical level, the tactical operative level. But at any rate, I did not have the possibility to give every single detail of my communication with the HVO to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would it also be true that in 1993, you frequently met with representatives of a variety of international organisations or concerns, including BritBat, UNPROFOR, and the European Community Monitors. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: These organisations that you enumerated, I did meet with them. I don't know if you mean any others, like Doctors Without Borders, and there were some other organisations represented, I don't recall all their names any more. But we also met with the UNPROFOR, UNHCR, the International Red Cross, and some others. Those were our frequent contacts in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And General, if any of those agencies or organisations had passed on information concerning alleged violations of the law by units of the 3rd Corps, would you have conveyed that information to the corps commander, General Hadzihasanovic, as well?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meetings of the joint commission, regardless of which particular joint commission it was, whenever we would receive information from international organisations about an incident or a criminal offence committed by a member of the BH Army, I always asked to be taken to that spot, to the crime scene, to see exactly what happened. And in such cases when we found that something indeed had taken place, we would always take steps. If it was found that a crime had occurred, I would always inform Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond the command of the 3rd Corps upon return from such meetings. We would always go on-site, and I have already spoken about this. Whenever I was informed that a crime or an offence had taken place, I would go myself to that spot to see where it had happened. We could only use UNPROFOR vehicles and their means of communication because there was no other way. I could not call my corps command from those meetings because there was no communication. I was only able to inform the commander of the key problems that I heard about at these meetings only upon return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us last week that in order to ensure that the law was complied with, the leadership of the 3rd Corps worked with the prosecutors and courts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military prosecutor's office and military courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have, to your recollection, any involvement with the civilian courts or the civilian prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally had no contact with them. Whether the commander of the corps had any, I don't know. When I spoke about the way I saw the military police, I explained that the military police was in charge of investigating infractions of discipline because it was their job. It was their job to make police reports and submit them to the prosecutor's office. It was not directly in my area of competence. You would have to ask the military police and the security organ who was in that business and whose job it was to take such measures. It was not my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, soldiers of the 3rd Corps should have been prosecuted by the district or within the district military court system. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in the area, and I don't think I can give you an answer to this. I don't even have enough information to give you the kind of answer you want. I can't reply really. It's not my field of expertise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. If you don't know, I certainly don't want you to speculate, but I have a few more questions along the same lines and if you know anything about it or you can help us in any way, it would be appreciated, but if you don't know, that's okay as well. Let me ask you if you were aware of any instances where soldiers of the 3rd Corps were tried by the civilian courts and that was later found to be an error because they should have been tried within the military courts.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. In fact, I'm not aware of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, or did you see at any point any documents or certificates sent by the 3rd Corps to the courts - the civilian courts or the military courts - confirming that an individual was a member of the 3rd Corps or one of its subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this question. Could you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we've had testimony before this Trial Chamber that in certain instances where a court was unable to determine if the perpetrator was a civilian or a member of the army, that certificates from the army would be a way for the court to determine if the perpetrator was a civilian or a soldier. And my question is: Do you recall any certificates like that being sent by the 3rd Corps to any of the courts within the 3rd Corps' zone, informing the court that the person was either a soldier or not a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall any such case. I don't know whether there were any, but I can't say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn now, sir, to a different topic. You told us last Monday that among the various groups - and this was early on, in 1992 - among the various groups prior to the formation of the 3rd Corps, you told us about the Patriotic League. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. I said there were units who had organised themselves as patriots to defend Bosnia-Herzegovina because it was the beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was the month of April. Even before this state of impending danger of war was proclaimed by the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina in early April 1992, there were clear indicators of aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially in the northeast. The aggressor was already carrying out specific operations and crimes were being committed against the civilian population. The country was preparing to defend itself, but at that point we still did not have an armed force ready to repel the attack so we relied on self-organised units. I also mentioned another organisation, the Patriotic League. When the Presidency gave the order that all the self-organised, self-initiated units place themselves under the command of the armed forces, I remember one of such organisations was the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us exactly what the Patriotic League was?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Patriotic League was an organisation that united patriots of Bosnia-Herzegovina in defence in case of attack by an aggressor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, were you involved in forming a Patriotic League as early as February 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did take part for the area of Zenica in February of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, there was a meeting on the 7th and 8th of February 1992 in Mehurici, and the point of that meeting was to coordinate regional plans for the Patriotic League and to assign tasks among the various attendees. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those assignments concerned defence against possible aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina. We had already been in possession of information that the Yugoslav People's Army was arming members of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. We heard that a great deal of weapons and military equipment had been transported into Bosnia-Herzegovina from Slovenia and Croatia and that these weapons and equipment were being distributed only among Serbs. And it was said at that meeting that we should prepare for defence, and if it comes to the worst, we should defend Bosnia and Herzegovina against the Yugoslav Army that was still present in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, among the people who attended this meeting on the 7th and 8th of February 1992 were the following, in addition, of course, to yourself: Sefer Halilovic, Alija Izetbegovic, Vahid Karavelic, and the Mufti of Travnik, Nusret Avdibegovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. This information you have is not correct. This meeting was not attended by late Alija Izetbegovic or the Travnik Mufti. I did attend, as well as General Sefer Halilovic and General Vahid Karavelic, but the Mufti and Mr. Izetbegovic were not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, in fact, you were responsible for organising the Patriotic League in 12 municipalities in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that some of the units that eventually -- some of the units that were formed within the 3rd Corps, in fact, grew out of these Patriotic League -- local Patriotic League units?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not be fair to say. The 3rd Corps grew out of Territorial Defence units. Already by that time, it was already operating as the Territorial Defence was able to operate. I already mentioned the great problems we encountered at the time. I don't want to repeat myself. But the 3rd Corps, as I said, grew out of Territorial Defence units that only transformed themselves into different organisations. They received additional manpower and additional newly mobilised units, starting from the Patriotic League and those patriotic forces which joined at a much earlier stage. That was not the factor that led to the appearance of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have phrased my question in a slightly different way. The units or the groups of people that were part of the Patriotic League, once the Territorial Defence units were formed, did the Patriotic League units simply disband? Did they, in effect -- large numbers of those people joined the local Territorial Defence units? Or what happened to these Patriotic League units that you set up in 12 municipalities in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't say that the patriotic forces for the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina were organised through the Patriotic League. There Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond were other patriotic organisations. I've already mentioned this. There were the Green Berets. As far as I know, there were some forces with the MOS insignia. They had various names. I don't know all of them. But I know that there was a Patriotic League organisation in 12 municipalities. These weren't units. They consisted of people who had joined those units. They didn't have weapons, they didn't have equipment. These were small groups of people. In 12 municipalities, there were perhaps between 30 to 40 people in each municipality. There weren't units. It's true that after the decision of the BH Presidency that all patriotic forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina should be placed under the Territorial Defence command, it's true that after this decision was taken, the Patriotic League followed it. But they were disbanded. They weren't placed under the command of the Territorial Defence, and in fact we did not have units of the Patriotic League any more, we had the Territorial Defence. And there were no Patriotic League units, in fact; there were people who had organised themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you say the Patriotic League was disbanded. Did those people that were in the Patriotic League then become members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people who wanted to be placed under the command of the Territorial Defence, those who wanted to join the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time did join the Territorial Defence. But there were some people who didn't. There were some people who didn't become members of the Territorial Defence. One couldn't say that they disbanded because this wasn't a strict organisation with its members. So it was a very unstable organisation. There wasn't much time to consolidate this organisation. So it's very difficult to talk about these people who were members of the Patriotic League in this way, as if they represented some sort of organised unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you've also mentioned several times and in two different contexts the Muslim armed forces, or MOS. We have also heard the term in this trial "Muslim forces" or "MS." Were these one and the same, or were there two different groups, one known as M-O-S and one known as M-S?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I had never seen a MOS unit or a Muslim forces unit. I said that I had information of the existence of such groups in the field. This is what they called themselves. I also said that the enemy propaganda made significant contributions. Later, we noticed that the HVO also had such propaganda objectives. I have testified before this Tribunal that at the highest level of the HVO, it was said that we were the Muslim forces, that we weren't in fact the ABiH, we were in fact Muslim forces. We protested as a result, and I have also mentioned Mr. Siber Stjepan, who is a Croat, as far as I know. They told him quite openly that he was a commander of the Muslim forces. I mentioned how Mr. Stjepan Siber reacted to this claim. I never saw a MOS group or a Muslim forces group. There were various names and the propaganda was of various types. These were claims that were made. But there were no MOS units in the Territorial Defence or in the 3rd Corps later on. And similarly, there were no Muslim forces in the Territorial Defence or within the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, a couple of follow-on questions with respect to what you've just told us. If I were to then therefore see a document of the HVO making reference to the MOS, would that, in fact, be a reference to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the HVO was referring to. But when such terms were used, for example, that there were MOS units or Muslim forces in the 3rd Corps, well, I would reject the use of such terms. I knew that this was just propaganda and I would always react decisively to such claims. I knew for sure that within the Territorial Defence, and later on within the 3rd Corps, there were no units called MOS or the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, just to finish with this specific aspect as it relates to the HVO, you've told us that the HVO referred to the 3rd Corps at times as being the MOS. And so my question was, if you see a document of the HVO that says "the MOS," would it follow that they were referring to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the HVO never said that the 3rd Corps was the MOS. They said that the 3rd Corps were the Muslim forces. The MOS and the Muslim forces, well, the difference is huge. These are different concepts. I don't know what you mean when you use these terms. They did say that the 3rd Corps consisted of the Muslim forces or were the Muslim forces, but they never said the 3rd Corps was identical to MOS. As far as I know, they only said that the 3rd Corps represented in fact the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Which, sir, gets me back to the question I asked you earlier: If there was a difference between the MOS and the Muslimanske Snage. And if there was a difference, if you could perhaps explain that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've testified before this Tribunal on a number of occasions and said that I had never seen the MOS or the Muslim forces, so I couldn't explain the difference between these two terms. I don't know how to explain this difference if I only heard rumours. I didn't see such units in the field. I wasn't able to examine the structure, see who the members were, who the members of the MOS and the Muslim forces were. This is an absurd question for me. It's all on the level of hypothesis. I can't testify about things I know nothing about. I don't know what the difference between the MOS and the Muslim forces would be. I wouldn't be able to say whether there is any such difference. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the reason I ask is because on page 23, line 16 and 17, just a few moments ago, the transcript of what you said is as follows: "The MOS and the Muslim forces, well, the difference is huge." And that could be an error, I don't know, because, unfortunately, I don't speak your language, but now you've said you don't know what the difference between the MOS and the MS would be, whereas just a moment ago the transcript recorded you saying there was a huge difference. So my question is: Was the MOS and the Muslimanske Snage the same thing or different things; and if they were different, could you please explain to us what the difference is.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I initially said that there was a difference, later you put detailed questions about this subject to me, well, I meant that MOS consists of three words, Muslim forces consists of two words. That's the difference I was referring to. I couldn't say what MOS is or what the Muslim forces were. I really couldn't say. I can't tell you about things I know nothing about. I don't know what you want me to say now. I could say that I knew such an organisation if it existed, if I had seen those people, if I knew those people, if I knew what their objectives were. In such a case then I could tell you about the difference. But I don't know what their objectives were, I don't know what the ideas were that the MOS and the Muslim forces had. But this is something that is intangible for me. I can't talk about something that I couldn't see or something that I had no contact with. I only heard rumours. I've mentioned the occasions on which I came across these terms. But when I mentioned the difference, I said why I thought there was a difference. The terms used are different. The MOS is a term that is different from Muslim forces. Perhaps it's the term "Muslim" that is the term that is the common one. If you ask me what armed forces are, I could answer that question, too. But as to what the Muslim forces are and as to what the MOS is, I don't know. I never saw such organisations, I never came across them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it, sir, then, if I were to ask you who was in the MOS or who was in the Muslimanske Snage, you wouldn't be able to assist us with that either.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't answer that question because I don't know what their objectives were. You might tell me that there was such-and-such a person who was present there. If you mention his name, I might be able to answer your question, but I don't know what the ideas or objectives of such a man might be. It's only after I've spoken to a certain individual that I could tell you about his objectives and ideas. I may have met Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond certain individuals, but I haven't discussed the subject of such individuals' objectives. I can't answer a question that's abstract. I can answer specific questions, concrete questions. I can answer questions about what I personally saw or what I have direct knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, this might be an appropriate time for our first technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's half past 3.00. We'll have our usual break. We'll resume at about 5 to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume, and I give the floor to Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me ask you just a few more questions concerning the subject we were talking about before the break, and then we'll move on. Earlier this afternoon, you mentioned a MOS insignia. That was at page 21, line 4. Do you recall ever seeing the MOS insignia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that I saw a MOS insignia. If I did say so, I was referring to information according to which there were groups called "the MOS." That's what I was told. But I don't remember saying that I actually saw MOS insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My question was if you saw any -- the answer was, you said: "As far as I know, there were some forces with the MOS insignia." That's what the English transcript says. And so my question was, did you ever see that? And I think you've told us that you may have had that information now, but my question is did you ever see any person or persons wearing a MOS insignia on their clothing?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that's what I said, then that was a mistake. I apologise. I had such information, but I did not actually see MOS units, nor did I see the sort of insignia they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you ever recall seeing any documents of the municipal defence staff or district staff making reference to the MOS or MS in late 1992 or early 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. But I wouldn't exclude that possibility. It would be necessary for me to see the document in question to see whether it's a document from the regional staff. I'd have to see the document in order to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps tomorrow we'll have the opportunity to look at some of such documents. I was just asking you now if you recalled seeing any such documents. Now, sir, do you know whether any of the person or persons who were with the MOS were subsequently in any units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I knew members who were in the Patriotic League. I also said that there were various such patriotic organisations. I don't know all of them. I could tell you about the people who were in the Patriotic League organisation, but I couldn't tell you anything about other organisations which I did not see. I only came across people from the Patriotic League. So as far as the Patriotic League is concerned, I can ask you [as interpreted] questions about this organisation. But as for the other patriotic forces, I couldn't tell you anything about them. I wasn't with them and I don't know the people who were members of these various patriotic organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that, for example, with respect to the MOS insignia, you said you had some information about that. Can you recall any of the other information that you had about the MOS or the Muslimanske Snage and where that information came from?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to the Trial Chamber. Perhaps I made a mistake. I don't know what kind of insignia these people wore. I never had occasion to see these people who were in a group or in some kind of an organisation or who had organised themselves in some other way. I wasn't in a position to see the sort of insignia that they wore. If I said I saw MOS insignia, I made a mistake. I apologise. I had information according to which there were people who had organised themselves on a patriotic basis, and they called themselves MOS, but I never saw such people, and I couldn't tell you anything about their insignia because I never had the opportunity of seeing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, my question is, again, you just told us that you had information according to which there were people who had organised themselves and called themselves MOS. Do you recall any of the specific information, other than what you just told us in very brief terms, about the MOS?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I've already provided you with details about the first time that I received information on the existence of groups that called themselves the MOS. This occurred in a very difficult and complex situation, and Your Honours, I have to repeat this to make sure that I am correctly understood. When the aggressor took Jajce and when he was very successful in the battlefield in the direction of Travnik on the Vlasic plateau, and close to Karaula, in these areas there was fierce fighting for every inch of land, for every house. People joined the fight to defend their homes. A lot of people had come from Krajina, from the surroundings of Banja Luka. There were a lot of people who had come from Jajce. There was the Jajce Territorial Defence that was completely dispersed. The situation was chaotic. It's difficult for me to make you understand what the situation was like, but it was very complex. I had information according to which everyone was involved in the fighting and according to which there was a group that called themselves the MOS. I didn't see them, but as I have said, later I tried to find out something about them. I also said that I had information at the time, at the beginning of November, according to which there were some foreigners who were assisting the people in defending their homes, in defending the Muslims in that area. But I didn't know who they were, how many of them there were, or where they were. All I knew was at that point in time, they were present in the area. This is something that I have testified about before this Court, and I can repeat all of this if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what you knew about the MOS unit that was in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the existence of a MOS unit in Travnik. I said that I had information according to which there were groups that had organised themselves for the defence of Karaula, and they called themselves the MOS. That's the information I had, but I did not see those forces. I didn't see that MOS unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, we have a bundle of documents that we would like to use for cross-examination purposes, and we do have sufficient copies for everyone in the courtroom. I'd ask that those be distributed now. As will become apparent once these are distributed, all of the documents in this bundle are Prosecution exhibits, and we have tabbed them in numerical order based on the Prosecution number. That's not necessarily the order we'll be reviewing them in, but they are tabbed numerically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you first, please turn to Prosecution Exhibit P695.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get the number. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P695. I ask you, sir, just to take a moment to take a look at this document, and then I'll ask you a couple of questions about this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've found the document, and I've had a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on your previous answer, I assume that you've never seen this document before. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, can you remind us what position you held on 15 September 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of September 1992, I was commander of the district staff of defence for the region of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I would ask you, if you could, just look down the list of the 80 individuals whose name appears on this document. And I would Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond like you, once you've done that, just to indicate that you've done so.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen the document and read the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how many, if any, of these people listed under numbers 1 through 80 do you know?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know one man from this list, if that is indeed the person I know something about. As for the others on the list, they're generally not familiar to me. Maybe I've heard something about a few of them at some point, but I may really know only one person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, would the person that you know on this list be Abdula Makteuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the person under number 1, Ahmet Adilovic, if that is the Ahmet Adilovic whom I had occasion to meet. The name coincides; the year of birth as well. Maybe there are other people who happen to be called Ahmet Adilovic and have the same father's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, how do you know Ahmet Adilovic? In what context or what capacity do you know Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't meet him on the 15th September 1992. I met him later, in Zenica, and I had occasion to see him. He told me that he was an Efendi by occupation, and I believe he told me then that he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade. At least, that's what he said. And again, I met him several times after the war, and I believe that he was working in a religious school, Medresa, after the war. If that is indeed the same person, the same Ahmet Adilovic, then he is the one I know from this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me approximately when Mr. Adilovic told you that he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade? The year and month, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it was in 1993. I can't remember the month, but it could be the first half of 1993. But certainly not in 1992. I didn't know him in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the transcript, can you tell us what an Efendi is.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: An Efendi is a man with religious training and education who is at the head of a community in a certain area. He leads prayers in that area which Muslims called dzemat. You can say that he is the leader of religious people at certain stages of prayer. I later found out that he had graduated from theological schools, and that is probably why they put him at the head of a Medresa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know the second person listed on this document, Abdula Makteuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Recently, I've had an opportunity to read about him because it is a name that has appeared frequently in the press in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As far as I was able to understand from media reports, it seems that there are proceedings against him going on, on suspicion that he was involved in kidnappings of Croat nationals in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's what I learned from TV reports not long ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever hearing the name or knowing Mr. Makteuf in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to pronounce this name. I don't remember ever meeting this man. I can't recall meeting him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be the case in both 1992 and 1993; you don't recall meeting Mr. Makteuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same goes for 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it assist your memory if I were to tell you that Mr. Makteuf was born in Iraq and operated a video store in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doesn't ring a bell at all. I was living in the Republic of Croatia and did not visit any video rental, especially not during the war. I don't know exactly when he operated this video rental. I never go to such places. When I have any time to spare, I spend it differently. I don't go to discotheques at all. And it is quite certain that I have never been in such a discotheque which was owned or run by this person who, as you say, was from Iraq. I never had opportunity to get such information or to attend personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just so it's clear, I never mentioned anything about a discotheque. Mr. Makteuf operated a video rental shop.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's even more remote from my life. I rarely have the time even to read a good book, let alone watch a video. And I never saw a place where videos would be rented or sold. I don't know anything about this man. I later found out that he used to own a different kind of company, a company called Palma, which was in the broadcasting business, a totally different business. But I never knew that he ran a video rental.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of broadcasting business was Palma, and when did you find out that Mr. Makteuf ran this company?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know all the lines of business they were in. But it also involved commerce. There was a shop among the other properties of that company. And I only later heard that he was the owner of that company. Maybe he was an employee, but nobody had told me that he was the actual owner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But sir, just so that we're 100 per cent clear, you never met with Mr. Makteuf in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never met with Mr. Makteuf in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, too, is correct. To the best of my recollection, I didn't meet him even then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it assist your recollection if I were to tell you again that Mr. Makteuf was a rather large-set -- rather large man and that he was from Iraq. Do you remember meeting any such person in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking of 1992 and 1993, I met many, many people over those years, and it doesn't ring a bell at all when you tell me that he was a large-set man. It doesn't tell me anything. It's a very broad term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, General. I would ask you to look at the name listed under number 16 on Prosecution Exhibit P695. Do you know Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard the name. Never seen a person called Ramo Durmis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't tell us anything whatsoever about Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say anything because I don't know the man. I don't know who he is. I said exactly who I might know from this list, and that is that could be, if it is the same person, Ahmet Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, then, sir, none of the other names on P695 are familiar to you, nor do you have any recollection of meeting or knowing any of those people?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, except for Ahmet Adilovic, if it is indeed the person I know something about, if it's not an entirely different person. At least, if I was able to read this list fully, there are certain names that are familiar, but if you match the surnames with those names, I can't really identify any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, what exactly do you mean by "there are certain names that are familiar"? Can you help us out by what you mean there.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, for instance, I know another Adilovic, but I did my secondary school in Travnik and graduated in 1986. I graduated the four-year secondary school in Travnik, and I knew a lot of people with similar surnames. But the only person I can identify by both first and last name is Ahmet Adilovic. I have encountered some of these surnames taken separately before, but nobody matches by both name and surname. There are several Adilovics even on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, one final question about this document: The person who signed this document, Lieutenant Colonel Redzic, do you know that person or have you ever heard of that person?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know this man personally, and I can't remember meeting him. Maybe indeed I did meet him at some point. Maybe he can confirm whether we had met or not. You have to understand that situation that prevailed in that particular month, September 1992. I'm not sure that this document was drafted exactly when it says on the document. I was so busy, I couldn't always remember my own name. I spent all my time touring the field. You should ask this person whether he had ever met me, because I can't remember seeing him. I was the commander and everybody Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond knew me as such. I, in my turn, could not know everybody I came in contact with, and when I was touring a large region, people would point me out as the commander, so in that way, maybe this Redzic encountered me in the same way, or maybe I was pointed out to him so he can say that he knew me. But it would be a good idea for you to contact him and ask because I personally don't remember ever seeing this man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you this question because you've told us that there weren't a lot of trained, senior officers available within the 3rd Corps zone. And it would seem that if there was a lieutenant colonel in Travnik, that you may have encountered him at some point in time or may have known him because there probably weren't a great number of lieutenant colonels in Travnik in September 1992. That's why I asked that question.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're completely right in saying that if I only had known that there were lieutenant colonels in that staff in Travnik, I would have sent my military police officers to bring him to work for me. I didn't know a single lieutenant colonel, apart from myself. Only when General Hadzihasanovic showed up, he was the second in that rank that I knew. If I was aware of this person's existence at the time, I would have literally sent military police to fetch him to work for my staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, one last question about this document, I hope: You just said, and this is at line 20 on page 35: "I'm not sure that this document was drafted exactly when it says on the document." I'm wondering what the basis for that statement was since you've told us that you never saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt what you're saying. I have complete trust in you, and if you say that that is indeed a genuine document that you marked as P695, I believe that you found it where you say you found it. I am taking your word for it. I have no particular reason to deny it, but I am indeed seeing it for the first time. I assert that strongly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to move on now to a different topic, and that topic is the mujahedin --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before you move on, because we might forget later, I have one question. Witness, could you please look at the last page of this document. You've seen that there is a stamp here with writing in Arabic that I cannot decipher. And then below, it says "Muslim forces." There is a saber drawn, and the number 3. Can you tell us whether one can conclude, based on this stamp, that it is a military stamp of any type?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As commander of the staff at the time, I can state with full responsibility that the Territorial Defence did not have such a stamp, and I can also state with equal certainty that this stamp has nothing to do with Territorial Defence or the staff of Territorial Defence of the Municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that was not the meaning of my question. This stamp does not look as a military stamp, particularly as it is bearing number 3. We have heard before a witness, a high-ranking military officer, who explained to us that military stamps bore numbers 1, 2, and 3, with 1 meaning the supreme, highest ranking commander; number 2 meaning deputy or assistant; whereas number 3 stood for chief of staff. Since we see the number 3 here, what can you tell us about this? Because this stamp is rather elaborate, and the person who made it must have followed certain rules in manufacturing the stamp. I'm asking you as a general of the army, does this stamp tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I state with full responsibility that, as you say, under the current system of command and control, numbers 1, 2, or 3 may designate officers of various ranks in the chain of command. But this stamp does not look to me as the stamp of armed forces, at least for the region of Travnik. I don't know about other regions. The legal staff, the legitimate staff of the armed forces in Travnik was our staff, and I can state with full responsibility that this is not the legitimate stamp of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That much, I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we're now going to turn to the issue of the mujahedin, or foreign fighters. You told us that the first time you ever saw any of the mujahedin was at the Guca Gora monastery in mid-June 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't know that they were mujahedin. But the first time I heard about the mujahedin was when I visited the village of Miletici. It was in mid-June near the church in Guca Gora that I first had the occasion of seeing such a group. I'm not sure whether this was a group of mujahedin, but I assume that that is what they were. Nevertheless, I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've talked about the presence of foreigners in the area, and I would like to try to draw a distinction between those foreigners who may have been there for humanitarian purposes and those foreigners who were there as fighters. And I would like to make this distinction because it's a little bit confusing from the transcript last week, when there are references to foreigners, whether those were fighters or humanitarian workers of some kind. And I'd like to ask you some questions to try to clarify that. When did you first become aware of the presence of foreign fighters - mujahedin - in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned an event that I participated in to an extent. This concerned the kidnapping of an HVO -- of an HVO officer in April 1993. According to information, we heard there were foreigners involved in the kidnapping who were in contact with the international community, and in particular, with the European monitors. When we noticed that this was being done by a group that wasn't under the control of the ABiH, or rather, that wasn't under the control of the 3rd Corps, this really demonstrated that there was a militant group of foreigners present in the area, and they weren't under the control of the 3rd Corps. This showed us that there was a group of foreigners that wasn't under the control of the 3rd Corps, and it was a group of military kind. I have spoken about this in detail. I spoke about this event before this Chamber last week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to the best of your recollection, sir, the first time you were aware of mujahedin in Central Bosnia was at or around the time Zivko Totic was kidnapped; middle of April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, we had intelligence and we had information obtained earlier on. But in fact, they weren't a problem for us. We weren't aware of this problem. As I said, I had information according to which a small group of foreigners had been observed in the course of 1992 in the month of November in the area of Karaula. I have also said that we had information according to which one group was engaged in lifting the blockade of Sarajevo, in December 1992. So we did have certain information, and our services tried to determine the identity of these people, but we weren't able to do so. And it was only when this HVO officer was kidnapped that a serious problem arose. But when this officer was kidnapped, at that time we weren't aware of the problem. We only found out about it subsequently, when the European monitors obtained more reliable information on the identity of those who had kidnapped this officer. They had obtained more reliable information than the information that the 3rd Corps had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we will spend a little bit of time either later this afternoon or again tomorrow talking specifically about the Totic kidnapping and the steps you took with respect to that kidnapping. I'm trying to focus now just on the issue of the mujahedin and when you became aware of them, and I think you've answered that question. At what point in time did the mujahedin become a problem for the 3rd Corps? Was it at the time of the Totic kidnapping? Was it at the time of the Miletici killings? Or was it at some other point in time? When did you and the corps commander come to the conclusion that the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond mujahedin were a problem or a significant problem in the 3rd Corps' area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said - I think I mentioned this last week - we realised that the presence of foreigners was a serious problem. I don't know whether they called them the mujahedin at the time. I wasn't even familiar with this term. I didn't know what it meant. And to this very day, I couldn't really explain to you the meaning of the term "mujahedin." I use the terms that are in current use. In the case of the events of Miletici, the Croats and the Serbs referred to the mujahedin. Trying to answer your question, this was a serious problem for us, the fact that there was a group of foreigners. There was a problem. I don't know what they called them, but this group of foreigners could be a serious problem for the 3rd Corps, and this is what took place when an HVO officer was kidnapped. This is when this problem arose. When this officer was kidnapped, on that day we didn't know the identity of the persons who had kidnapped him. We found out about his identity at a later date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, if I understand you correctly, you came to the conclusion that the mujahedin were a significant problem once you determined that they were responsible for the kidnapping of Zivko Totic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are using the term "the mujahedin." If you say that these foreigners were called the mujahedin, I will accept that. But I don't know who these foreigners were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what was the term that you used to describe these people? Was it simply "foreigners" or was it "Arabs" or was it "mujahedin"? What term do you feel most comfortable using? And I will adapt my questions to avoid causing any confusion.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope that we can use one term to refer to the same group of people, to a group of people who share similar characteristics. This will help us to avoid any confusion. I'll accept the term that you decide to use. Then I'll know what you are referring to when you put a question to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would actually rather do it the opposite way. You tell me what term you prefer to use or which term you used at the time, in 1993, to discuss these people or to refer to these people, and I will use that word or term.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, I thought that this was a group of people from countries in the East. Later, I heard that people would call them the mujahedin. So we can speak about this event in such terms. I'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I must intervene because you are inverting the question. The Prosecution is asking you to say how you would describe them, and you are saying, no, you say whatever you like and I'll follow your usage. But the Prosecution wants to know how you called them at the time. That is the question being put to you. So please, answer the question. Say you didn't have a name for them, or you called them "the Arabs" or you called them "mujahedin" or you called them "X," "Y," or "Z." This is what we would like to hear. We don't want to hear what the Prosecution calls them and then have you use the same term. You are being asked this, not the Prosecution. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do understand. Before I heard the term "the mujahedin," I used the expression "a group of foreigners."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I will use the term "a group of foreigners," to refer to these people, but I want to also avoid any confusion that this group of foreigners included humanitarian workers. Do you understand the difference that I'm trying to make?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand the distinction you are making.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we're clear then, prior to April 1993, you didn't consider that there were any problems with the foreigners in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were requests. This is something I have testified about. There were some people, or foreigners, who were detained in HVO prisons. And when there were discussions with the HVO, because that was the only way of communicating with the HVO, there were requests from the Ministry of the Interior and from humanitarian organisations, and it was said that they were looking for foreigners. I have testified about this already. But when there were these searches for foreigners, well, these requests for communication with the HVO went through me. There were a few people, three, four, five, I think, I don't know how many exactly, but we received requests to seek for such foreigners. I don't know what capacity they were there in, but there was such a group of foreigners. But this wasn't a problem for the 3rd Corps; at least, not at the time.
